subject: SubstrateAI performance targets & deployment topology — next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@substrate.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up — performance goals, constraints and proposed next steps

Hi Sanjay / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time on yesterday's call. Wanted to capture the key outcomes and make sure we have the right engineers on the next technical session. Below is a concise summary plus concrete next steps.

TL;DR
- Primary ask: reduce unpredictable tail latency while keeping unit-cost within your target band.
- Target SLOs discussed: p95 latency <= 150ms for chat requests; sustained throughput target ~600 req/s at peak with brief spikes to 1k; cold-start recovery < 500ms for cached prefixes.
- Constraints: 16k context support, streaming responses, strict data residency for EU-born customers (GDPR), and HIPAA-adjacent controls for certain workflows.

What we heard (pain + impact)
- Latency spikes during peak hours (even with autoscaling) are causing session timeouts and increased user abandonment (estimated 8–12% lost conversions).
- Cost volatility because current provider can’t leverage prefix/KV caching or continuous batching efficiently for your prompt mix.
- Model trade-off: you need open-model flexibility (70B-class for accuracy on product copy tasks) but want a quantized fallback to control cost.

Technical notes / assumptions from the call
- Traffic profile: 85% chat inference (short prompts, many continuations), 15% long-context batch-generation for synthesis reports.
- KV-cache pattern: high reuse on welcome/adaptive prompts — expected hit rate target 65–75% after warm-up.
- Region: primary workloads in us-west1, EU residents must stay in europe-west1 cluster when identified as EU users.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level)
- Deployment topology: hybrid dedicated GPU pool for primary (A100 80GB class, quantized Llama-2-70B variant for the high-quality path) + warm-standby smaller nodes (H100 or T4 for scaled throughput) and CPU fallback for best-effort requests.
- Performance levers: prefix/KV caching tuned per prompt family, workload-aware batching thresholds, and model-variant routing with automatic fallback based on SLO violations.
- Observability: token-level latency breakdown, per-route p50/p95/p99, KV hit/miss charts, and per-request trace ids for debugging.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
1) Schedule a 90-min technical deep-dive with your infra/SRE and our SEs — proposed window: Thurs 09/16 or Mon 09/20. (Action: Marissa to coordinate calendar)
2) You to share a 48-hour sample of traffic (anonymized) + a few representative prompt sets and SLA/regions document. (Action: Sanjay / Priya)
3) Vivek to draft a topology sketch + initial sizing and an estimate for two options (quality-first and cost-first) by EOD Mon 09/20. (Action: Vivek)
4) I’ll upload a mutual action plan and attach the call recording and the metric export.

Attachments: call-recording-20260913.mp3 (audio stub), substrateai-metrics.csv (sample traffic), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (working plan)

If that's accurate, please reply with which deep-dive slot works and any additional constraints (e.g., encryption/HSM requirements).

Thanks,
Olga
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Looping in high-level topology notes that I'll walk through in the deep-dive. Rough sizing/assumptions (will refine with their traffic sample):

Assumptions- avg tokens per chat req: 120
- avg tokens per long job: 4,500
- target sustained throughput: 600 req/s (chat), peak 1,000 req/s for short bursts
- desired p95 chat latency: <=150ms

Option A — Quality-first (recommended for initial pilot)- Model: Llama-2-70B FP16 -> quantized-aware kernels where possible- Hardware: 4 x A100-80GB per shard (multi-instance GPU packing)- Topology: 3 primary shards, continuous KV caching layer (shared Redis-like L2 with local warm caches), autoscaling floor 2 shards, burst to 5 shards- Expected p95: 80–140ms (workload dependent)- Pros: accuracy, simple routing; Cons: cost higher

Option B — Cost-first (recommended for scale trials)- Model mix: 35B quantized as primary, 70B quality path for high-confidence queries via model-variant routing- Hardware: mix of A100-80GB + T4 pool for quantized instances; CPU fallback for background/async jobs- Expected p95: 120–180ms on quantized path, 90–130ms on 70B path for routed requests

KV-cache & batching notes
- We can implement prefix normalization and bloom-filtered KV keys to reduce cold-start blowups. With proper normalization I expect hit-rate improvements from ~40% -> 60–75% in 24–48 hours of traffic.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batch-sizing with latency SLO guardrails; we keep a fast-path for streaming chat to avoid batching delays >20ms.

EU/Residency
- Use region-tagged routing at the API layer to guarantee processing in eu-west1 for flagged requests. Keep model weights replicated or use a read-local inference tier for EU customers to avoid cross-region egress.

Attached: quick ascii sketch of the flow

[Client] -> API Gateway (tenant+region router) -> Router (quality vs cost variant) -> KV-cache (local warm cache + L2 shared) -> GPU pool (shard pool) -> Fallback CPU pool

I'll prepare a cost delta spreadsheet and an expected token-cost per option before the call. Need: sample payloads and representative concurrency matrix (requests/sec per prompt family).

— Vivek
